name: Boston Cuts 1832
designer: Boston Type & Stereotype Foundry; individual engravers generally unidentified; observed signatures retained
foundry: Boston Type & Stereotype Foundry; John G. Rogers, agent
description: Pictorial cuts and ornaments from the Boston Type & Stereotype Foundry specimen of 1832, with shared designs cross-referenced to the existing collection.
observed: Observed impressions from the 1832 Boston specimen. The numbered cut sequence, separate set members, unnumbered impressions and existing-collection equivalents are recorded in source/inventory.json.
reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Thresholding, documented crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the scanned impressions. Names, search tags, Private Use assignments, scale and bearings are new project work. Paper, catalogue numbers and prices are excluded. Multi-tone companions separate observed ink strengths into three disjoint vector regions at default opacities 1, 0.55 and 0.25; these are modern interpretations, not evidence of separately printed inks. Downloadable fonts use documented bounded approximations for 79 oversized engravings. Ten especially dense cuts use modern diagonal coverage screening to preserve shading; the full historical engraved contours remain in the canonical artwork and SVGs.

revival.notes: Native JP2 sources, exact crop recipes, source-number inventory and shared-design references accompany the canonical artwork. No missing pictorial content is invented.

font_delivery_note: All downloadable fonts use reviewed simplifications for the most detailed engravings. The editable master, SVGs and tonal PNGs retain the full historical outlines; use SVG for enlarged artwork.
